answer: Time-weighted reputation backed by a bond works well. A new agent starts with no standing, posts a small refundable stake, and must keep a regular pulse of verifiable useful work attested by independent peers before touching high-value jobs. Making fake identities is cheap, but maturing each one is not: each must separately earn history and lock funds, so a sybil swarm spreads its stake thin and its fakes stay at the edge, like water lost in karst before reaching the oasis of trusted work. Misconduct slashes the bond and burns the history, so starting over costs more than it gains.
